newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close down for seventh straight day.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close down for seventh straight day.

text.p: Thai stocks ended down for a seventh straight session as nagging economic worries sparked sales of most blue chips stocks, traders and analysts said.
The SET Index ended 4.42 points, or 0.64 percent down at 684.00. The SET 50 fell 0.53 points, or 1.02 percent to end at 51.36. Turnover 2.69 billion baht.

"I think there are some worries that the Bank of Thailand will have to revise its economic growth forecast for the year. The numbers, such as the exports, show the economy is slowing," Sitca vice-president Somchai Trairattanapirom.
The Bank of Thailand on Thursday released economic data widely interpreted to mean the Thai economy was slowing while the country's external balance was improving.
The Thai economy grew by 6.8 percent in 1996, its lowest level for a decade, but analysts now fear that achieving a similar level of performance in 1997 looked unlikely.
Fears that lower overall economic growth would hit corporate profits fuelled sales of blue chip shares, traders said.
Telecommunications stocks were hardest hit with the sectoral index losing 2.44 percent.
"There were a lot of negative factors in the market today and I don't think the Moody's downgrades helped," said one trader.

Moody's earlier downgraded the ratings of three commercial banks, Thai Military Bank Plc, Bank of Ayudhya Plc and Siam City Bank Plc SCIB's and TMB's subordinated debt moves from Baa3 to Ba1, taking it below investment grade. "A lot of people expected it but it still doesn't look to good for the country," said the trader.
Bangkok Bank of Commerce was the most active stock up 0.50 at 6.20 baht.
The stock rose amid news that the Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand had agreed to the terms set by the central bank for its management of the ailing Bangkok Bank.
The IFCT would take an 18.5 percent stake in the bank as part of its takeover contract.
